intro: Fabian Wöhrle plays Buxtehude’s Praeludium in C major, BuxWV 137. It opens with a passage for the pedals alone, which is followed by a fugue and then a quick chaconne over a repeating bass.

sections.label: Intro · The pedals begin alone
sections.mNote: Four bars for the feet before the hands join.

sections.label: A · Fugue on the pedal figure
sections.mNote: The opening pedal figure becomes the fugue subject.

sections.label: Link · Free passagework over pedals
sections.mNote: The last fugue entry leads into free running notes.

sections.label: B · Chaconne on a three-bar ground bass
sections.mNote: Eight statements of the ground beneath changing upper parts.

cues.title: Opening pedal solo
cues.text: For four bars the organist plays with the feet alone. The pedal line moves by leaps and in runs that turn back on themselves, and the hands rest. The first notes on the manuals come near the end of bar five.
cues.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 1–5: pedal solo, with the first manual notes late in bar 5. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Abendmusiken, Marienkirche, Lübeck
cues.text: Buxtehude took up the organist’s post at Lübeck’s Marienkirche in 1668. Alongside the services, he developed the church’s public evening concerts, the Abendmusiken. From 1678 these included sacred dramatic works.
cues.evidence: Marienkirche’s historical account gives the 1668 appointment and the sacred dramatic Abendmusiken from 1678. https://www.st-marien-luebeck.de/en/music/dieterich-buxtehude

cues.title: Fugue, bars 36–64
cues.text: The quick figure from the pedal solo now passes from voice to voice in a fugue. Relf Clark connected the subject with bar 2 of the pedal solo. Each earlier voice continues to play when the next one enters.
cues.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 36–64. Relf Clark connects the fugue subject with bar 2 of the pedal solo. https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Bach’s visit to Lübeck, 1705
cues.text: In 1705 Bach went to Lübeck to hear Buxtehude. His employers in Arnstadt had granted four weeks’ leave, and he stayed away for four months. On his return he had to explain the absence to the church authorities.
cues.evidence: Marienkirche’s account quotes Bach’s obituary and the Arnstadt consistory minutes of 21 February 1706. https://www.st-marien-luebeck.de/en/music/dieterich-buxtehude

cues.title: Manual passagework after final fugue entry
cues.text: The last fugue entry leads without a break into rapid runs on the manuals. The pedals alternate moving notes with long-held ones. Above them, the hands exchange scales.
cues.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 64–74; Relf Clark identifies the unbroken continuation from the final subject entry. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf ; https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Chaconne, from bar 75
cues.text: The Presto Ciacona is a fast dance in triple metre. A three-bar bass pattern is heard eight times, and the parts above it change with each statement. The ground is derived from the fugue subject, which is itself derived from the opening pedal solo.
cues.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), from bar 75, marked Presto Ciacona in 3/2. Relf Clark identifies the eight statements and the ground’s relation to the subject. https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Reiser organ, Gerstetten, 1984
cues.text: Fabian Wöhrle plays the Reiser organ of the Catholic church of St Peter and St Paul in Gerstetten. Built in 1984, it has two manuals, pedal and 22 stops.
cues.evidence: The Commons description of this recording names the performer, the church and the Reiser organ, II/P/22, 1984 (two manuals, pedal, 22 stops): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:D._Buxtehude_Pr%C3%A4ludium,_Fuge_und_Chaconne_C-Dur_BuxWV_137_Fabian_W%C3%B6hrle_Kath._Kirche_Gerstetten.mp3

transitions.title: From the pedal solo into the fugue
transitions.to: A · Fugue on the pedal figure
transitions.how: The bass reaches C and the pedals stop. The fugue opens with a running figure on the manuals, taken from the shape of the opening pedal solo. Further voices enter one by one, and later the pedals play the subject again.
transitions.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 35–40. Relf Clark explains the subject’s origin in the pedal solo. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf ; https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201

transitions.title: Final fugue entry into free passage
transitions.from: A · Fugue on the pedal figure
transitions.how: The pedals take the last fugue entry, at bar 64, directly into the freer passage. Above them, the right hand plays a descending scale. More runs pass between the hands until the pedals hold a long G, keeping the music on the dominant of C.
transitions.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 64–74; Relf Clark identifies the final subject entry at bar 64. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf

transitions.title: Held G to the Presto Ciacona
transitions.to: B · Chaconne on a three-bar ground bass
transitions.how: The pedals hold G, the dominant of C major. At bar 75, marked Presto Ciacona, the metre changes to 3/2 and the pedals begin a three-bar ground on C. The hands play one chord and then rest while the pedals state the ground.
transitions.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 70–77, especially the G pedal and the change to Presto Ciacona at bar 75. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf
